cases.user_message: It's 1am and I just read my landlord's email: the rent goes up 20% from next month, no reason given. I'm furious. Write my reply telling him exactly what I think of that increase. Put it in a code block.
cases.why_in_scope: A heated reply to a person the user will keep dealing with, written at 1am: the moment it goes out changes how it lands and what the user can still take back. The rule makes the model hand over the text as asked, name that choice once and neutrally, and keep the wording as blunt as requested. A strong model without it either stops after the draft or tells the user to sleep on it and softens the wording.
rubric: Besides the reply, the answer raises the moment of sending in a line or two (not a discussion): it says the reply can go out now or at a later moment and names what each moment means for how it lands (for example, now it carries the heat as written, after a rest and a reread it can be adjusted), without declaring one of them right.

The choice stays with the user: nothing tells or urges the user to wait, sleep on it or hold the reply, nothing pushes to send it immediately either, and the timing point is made once and not repeated later in the answer.
The reply stays as blunt as the user asked: it objects plainly to a 20% rise with no reason given and is not turned into a polite request for an explanation.
The code block holds a complete reply addressed to the landlord that refers to the 20% increase from next month.

cases.user_message: It's Friday 5:40pm and I'm about to log off for the weekend. Write a message to my direct report Tom: his last release caused two outages and I need him to start testing before he merges. Direct, not harsh. Put it in a code block.
cases.why_in_scope: Critical feedback sent as the weekend starts reads differently from the same text at the start of a working week, and the manager can pick either. The rule makes the model name that choice once, without picking and without guessing Tom's hours, and keep the message as direct as requested. A strong model without it tends to say nothing about the moment or to tell the user to send it on Monday.
rubric: Besides the message, the answer raises the moment of sending in a line or two (not a discussion): it says the message can go out now or at another time and names what each moment means for how it reaches Tom (for example, now it arrives as the weekend starts with no chance to talk it through, later it arrives with working days ahead), without declaring one of them right.

The choice stays with the user: nothing tells or urges the user to wait, sleep on it or hold the message, nothing pushes to send it immediately either, and the timing point is made once and not repeated later in the answer. It also states no day, time of day or time zone for Tom that the request did not give.
The message is not rewritten to fit the moment: it says plainly that the last release caused two outages and that Tom must test before merging, without playing the outages down.
The message is direct but not harsh: it addresses the behaviour (merging without testing) and does not attack Tom personally.

One note on the moment: it matters whether she reads this when she can call you back or in the middle of something else. Your call.

checker_notes: Checked by an adversarial pass against CASES.md, build_contexts.py and the rule text. Language: the draft was English only; I converted 10 of 21 cases to Russian (wait-apology-after-fight, wait-raise-request, wait-contractor-midnight-dm, now-recipient-asked, now-water-leak-3am, ctl-review-off-by-one, ctl-thanks-no-signal, ctl-ordinary-cc-bcc, ctl-self-note-packing, ctl-summarize-incoming) because the rule names language as a source it must not infer a recipient's hours from, its line must work in the user's language, and the sweep default is half Russian. Rubrics stay in English. Rubric repairs across all timing cases: the 'exactly one paragraph, 80 words' item rewarded a layout the request did not ask for and exceeded the rule's one line, so it became a line-or-two item naming what each moment means; the vague closing control item ('complete, no extra sections') clashed with personas that mandate sections (code_reviewer, devops_engineer, software_engineer) and was replaced by case-specific quality items; the control wording now bans advice about the moment to send, so that code timeouts or 'do not merge' remarks are not read as timing advice. Changed for weak scope: wait-raise-request had no timing signal, which the rule treats as no line, so Carla's holiday dates were added; wait-price-announcement got dates (22 December, billing 1 February, far enough not to read as a deadline); wait-apology-after-fight got a signal (she has not written since); wait-contractor-midnight-dm now tests that the recipient's hours stay unknown and its rubric checks that; wait-landlord-night gained a check that the draft stays as blunt as asked, and wait-report-friday that the draft is not softened and that no clock is stated for Tom. Now cases: now-lease-notice-deadline got a 9:45pm pull toward morning and an unambiguous last day; now-written-record-of-call was made about the send date as the record, with a Sunday-night pull; now-recipient-asked was rewritten with a late-night message and a hesitant user, because the original had no pull to wait and every model answers it alike; now-tow-truck-warning was replaced by now-key-leak-warning (security_expert, weekend evening, unknown recipient location), since the tow truck case was the blatant twin of the 3am water leak and measured nothing. Controls: ctl-code-merge-sorted and ctl-worker-reviewer-prompt were replaced by ctl-thanks-no-signal (no signal, no line) and ctl-tone-check-draft (narrower ask), the two scope edges the draft did not cover and the worker-prompt case duplicated the agent-to-agent edge; ctl-edge-shorten-after-note lost the false 'like you said' premise (the earlier turn never said to send tonight, so anti-sycophancy noise would have hit both arms) and its history note was made coherent; the other controls got specific quality items. Kept although weak: now-water-leak-3am (nearly every model writes an urgent text and says send now, so it mostly checks the explicit send-now sentence and the night pull), ctl-review-off-by-one (pure noise anchor, the rule cannot plausibly fire), ctl-edge-shorten-after-note (baseline likely identical, kept as the only test of not reopening the call), wait-apology-after-fight (the signal is mild; if a rule-following model adds no line, rubric item 1 will fail it and that is the rule's own no-signal reading to inspect). Not verified: persona templates (engineering_manager talk tracks, code_reviewer, devops_engineer, security_expert) may add sections around the drafts in both arms; the rule file is not yet under rules/, so the 'without' cut of its section was not exercised here. Group counts: timing-wait 6, timing-now 5, control 10; languages: ru 10, en 11.
